Rapper Snoop Doggy Dogg Charged With Marijuana Possession
After Reporting Being Assaulted; Several Lessons

(Ed. note: This story illustrates one of the less understood side-effects of marijuana prohibition. If someone with marijuana becomes the victim of a real crime, they run a real risk of getting themselves in trouble if they report it to the police.

Also this is a case in which the police claim that smelling marijuana is grounds for a search.

Although possession of less than an ounce of marijuana in California is a misdemeanor, Mr. Dogg could be in violation of his probation and end up in prison for possession of marijuana.

Remember, he was the one who was assaulted. This encourages precisely the kind of vigilantism for which the Rap culture is criticized. If you can’t call the police, you take matters into your own hands. This is a "prohibition culture.")

Rapper Snoop Doggy Dogg cited for having pot

LOS ANGELES (Reuters) -
Rapper Snoop Doggy Dogg and his companion were cited for misdemeanor marijuana possession after an altercation backstage at a comedy show, a sheriff’s spokesman said Saturday.

The 34-year-old rapper—whose real name is Calvin Broadus—and Delmar Arnaud, 26, were each found with less an ounce of the drug and were not taken into custody, said Deputy Jim Hellmold.

Both men were ordered to appear in Beverly Hills Municipal Court July 1.

Hellmold said Broadus approached sheriff’s deputies backstage at the Universal Ampitheatre to report an altercation with a group of four to six men after his performance at the "Def Comedy Jam."

Broadus told the deputies that one of the men had slapped him, then fled, Hellmold said.

It was while taking the report, Hellmold said, that the deputies smelled marijuana on Broadus and Arnaud.

"The deputies came in contact with him (Broadus) and smelled marijuana," Hellmold said. "They searched him, found that he had less than an ounce, and cited and released him."

The incident was not Broadus’ first brush with the law.

Broadus and his bodyguard, McKinley Lee, were tried and acquitted of murder for the August, 1993 drive-by shooting of a 20-year-old gang member named Philip Woldermarian.

And he was placed on three years probation in March 1997 for illegal possession of a weapon.
